Topics.type1_consolidated:
## Appraisals
Students found several aspects of the Topics course praiseworthy. They appreciated that the course content was well-structured and engaging, with lively and energetic classes led by a good instructor. The Python part was particularly noted as being good, and the curriculum and syllabus were described as great. Additionally, the course content was praised for its design and the inclusion of fresh material. The lectures, discussions, and overall course structure were also highlighted as positives.

## Criticisms
One criticism was raised regarding the outdated nature of the course content, with some students feeling that the topics were not state-of-the-art. Another concern was the slow pace of the course, which was mentioned as a point for improvement. 

## Suggestions
Students suggested that the course should include more implementation-based discussions and demonstrations using Python notebooks, especially for theoretical concepts. There was also a suggestion to ensure that the course content remains up-to-date and relevant.
Topics.type2_positive: Students found several aspects of the Topics course praiseworthy, particularly the quality and organization of the course content, which they felt was well-structured and engaging. They appreciated the effective delivery of lectures and discussions, noting that the instructor made the sessions lively and interesting. Additionally, many students highlighted the relevance and freshness of the material covered, including Python, SQL & Relational Models, and specific topics like data types, conditionals, and Python modules. The overall positive sentiment reflects satisfaction with both the theoretical and practical components of the course.
Topics.type3_negative: Students found the course content outdated and criticized the topics for not being up-to-date with current advancements. They also expressed difficulties in applying theoretical concepts practically, suggesting the need for more tutorials and lab sessions to help them better understand and implement the material.

Organization.type1_consolidated:
## Appraisals
No feedback of this type.

## Criticisms
Students found the course to be highly stressful and lacking coherence between labs and lectures. They felt that the lab exercises were more difficult than the class content, leading to an unfair pressure on them. The course structure was described as chaotic and unorganized, with lectures not syncing well with labs and tutorials. Additionally, the difficulty of the labs spiked suddenly, and there was a mismatch between the material covered in theory classes and practical sessions.

## Suggestions
Students suggested extending quiz times to accommodate technical login lags and increasing the availability of practice sheets. They also recommended that TAs provide more support to students and ensure that the labs align better with the lecture content. Some students also called for a more systematic approach to course management and a better alignment between class and lab materials.
Organization.type2_positive: Students appreciated the well-managed and systematic nature of the course, which included thorough material, surprise quizzes, and frequent tests that effectively facilitated learning. They also highlighted the structured content and the overall organization of the course as significant factors in their educational experience. Additionally, the assignments were noted for developing essential skills, and the knowledgeable teaching assistants contributed positively to the learning environment.
Organization.type3_negative: Students found the organization of the course to be highly unsatisfactory, citing several key issues. They reported that the labs were significantly more difficult than the lectures, creating a stressful and high-pressure environment. There was also a lack of coherence between the labs and the class content, with labs often introducing concepts not covered in lectures. Additionally, the structure of the course was perceived as chaotic and unorganized, with lectures feeling rushed and lacking detail. Students also noted that the difficulty of the labs did not align with the simplicity of the lectures, leading to frustration and confusion. Overall, the disjointed nature of the course components and the mismatch between theoretical and practical aspects of the course were major sources of dissatisfaction.

They also suggested making compute resources more readily available and reducing the emphasis on hands-on DL knowledge that some students found challenging to master.
